# Raw Claim Document — Romer Solow Model (v1, pre-refinement)

This fixture represents a raw, under-specified decomposition of claims from
the Solow growth model chapter of an advanced macroeconomics text.
Claims are stated without explicit scope, without falsification conditions,
and with missing evidence types — intentionally deficient for descent testing.

## Claims

Capital accumulates over time.
Output is produced by combining capital and labor.
The savings rate determines the fraction of output that is invested.
Depreciation reduces the capital stock each period.
In the long run, the economy converges to a steady state.
Higher savings rates cause higher steady-state capital per worker.
Technology is exogenous.
All workers are human.
The production function exhibits diminishing returns to capital.
If the economy is below its steady state, it grows faster.

## Normative and Vague Claims

The economy should save more to maximize growth.
Capital ought to be allocated efficiently.
It could be said that growth is broadly determined by fundamentals.
One could argue that the model captures the essential dynamics.

## Overclaimed Causal Assertions

AI increases output in the same way labor does.
Replacing human workers with AI algorithms causes growth to accelerate.
The same diminishing returns that apply to human capital also apply to AI capital.
